text:
ana: Heads up — ran the analysis on shared runtime drift. Propose a 'service grooming' plan to extract two small runtimes and tighten contracts. quick thread.

mike: Can you share the high-level tradeoffs? risk of performance regressions?

ana: Tradeoffs: initial perf hit during cold start growth vs long-term faster deploys & smaller blast radius. We'll keep kernel selection same; only split the orchestration surface.

jia: Proposal sketch:
1) identify 3 candidate responsibilities (KV cache ownership, prefix caching API, session assignment).
2) extract as 'satellite' services behind a thin facade.
3) keep breathable compatibility layer for 6 months.

ravinder: How do we keep rollout safe? Also what's owner matrix?

ana: Rollout: design spike (2 weeks), implement extract with feature flags, canary 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> full. Auto-fallback to monolith on errors. Owners: runtime-team for core, platform-team for facade and routing, eng-sre for rollback policies.

katy: Need clear contract: request/response JSON and error semantics. Suggest explicit semver header and schema validation on facade.

jia: Agreed. Example header: `X-Svc-Contract: runtime.v1` and return `contract_error` code. We'll add unit tests to enforce.

mike: Can we avoid duplicate KV state? Cache coherence is scary.

ana: Yes — plan: maintain single canonical KV store (existing cache) and the satellite reads via read-through. Writes stay on core until we migrate. No dual-writes.

ravinder: Metrics we should track: latency P50/P95, error rate, dropped tokens, request amplification. Also cost delta per 100k tokens.

katy: I'll add eval prompts to Redwood Optimize to detect quality regressions during canary.

arch-bot: Created RFC doc: link https://redwood.internal/rfcs/2201-service-grooming (internal).

mike: Question on tech debt paydown: do we pay down infra debt first or interface debt?

ana: Parallel: small debt tickets tied to each extract (e.g., remove deprecated flags, simplify config). Larger infra rework queued after first extraction.

jia: Timeline suggestion: spike weeks 1-2, extraction weeks 3-6, canary ramp 7-10, cleanup & docs 11-12.

ravinder: Sounds good. I'll create tracking epic and assign owners. @katy you'll take contract validation?

katy: :thumbsup: will do. Posting checklist in the RFC.

ana: Thanks all. Last call: any blockers? If not, we'll kick off spike Monday.
